question: Is the air better in the north or the west of Singapore right now?
name: Claude
answer:
**The north has the better air.** The latest NEA readings I could find are from 7am on 17 Oct. I can't pull a live feed, so check NEA or myenv for the current numbers.

| Region | 24-hr PSI | 1-hr PM2.5 (µg/m³) |
|---|---|---|
| North | 144 | 83 |
| West | 181 | 97 |

At 7am, the 24-hour PSI was in the "unhealthy" range in all regions: central (191), north (144), south (161), east (175), west (181). Hourly PM2.5 readings stayed "elevated" across all regions at 7am: central (108), north (83), south (75), east (119), west (97).

- **North was cleaner in earlier readings too.** At 12pm on 16 Oct, one tracker showed the west at 202 (very unhealthy) against 153 (unhealthy) in the north.
- **The cause is regional haze.** Smoke from Kalimantan and southern Sumatra has kept readings high, so every region is still in the unhealthy range.
- **The outlook is poor.** NEA said the PSI forecast for Oct 17 could be between 150 and 230, from "unhealthy" to "very unhealthy".

Even in the north, the air is unhealthy. Healthy people should cut back on prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion. The elderly, pregnant women and children should limit time outdoors.

# Haze in Singapore: PSI back to ‘unhealthy’ range, PM2.5 remains ‘elevated’ in all regions
SINGAPORE - The hazy conditions continued in the morning of Oct 17 even as the 24-hour PSI in central Singapore dipped back to the "unhealthy" band after staying in the "very unhealthy" range the day before.

At 7am, the 24-hour PSI was in the "unhealthy" range in all regions: central (191), north (144), south (161), east (175), west (181).

The central region was worst hit on Oct 16 when the 24-hour PSI there registered "very unhealthy" readings throughout the day, peaking at a season high of 229 from 3pm to 4pm, till the early hours of Oct 17.



Air quality is considered "unhealthy" when the PSI – a 24-hour rolling average of six key air pollutants – is in the range of 101 to 200, and "very unhealthy" when it is in the range of 201 to 300.

Meanwhile, the hourly PM2.5 readings – measured in micrograms per cubic metre and used as a gauge for current air quality – remained in the "elevated" range across all regions at 7am: central (108), north (83), south (75), east (119), west (97).

In its daily haze advisory on the evening of Oct 16, the National Environment Agency (NEA) said the PSI forecast for Oct 17 could be between 150 and 230, putting it in the range of "unhealthy" to "very unhealthy".
